reason: A’s partial Hf→Zr substitution is the more physically credible density-reduction strategy because Zr is a lighter, chemically similar refractory element and is less likely than Al to induce ordering or brittle intermetallics that undermine high-temperature performance. A still needs a fixed substitution level, a quantitative density rejection threshold, and correction of the unsupported >50% baseline ductility claim, but B’s claimed ~10% density reduction and preserved phase stability from only 20% replacement of the Hf fraction are poorly grounded.
